description: The person and the coding agents in a workspace, working together through a small set of primitives: messages, a shared notebook, starting and stopping agents, and the IDE.
config.title: Facade Agents
config.enabled: Lets the person and the coding agents Facade starts work together: messages, a shared notebook, agents that start other agents, and the IDE. Off means Facade starts no server, writes nothing under ~/.facade/workspaces and launches no agents.
config.maxParallel: The most features that agents work on at the same time.
config.checkSlots: The most acceptance checks that run at the same time. Builds and test suites are heavy, so this is kept apart from the number of agents.
config.ladder: The agents a feature goes through, in order, when one fails its checks: for example `["codex", "claude:sonnet", "lead"]`. An entry is an agent id with an optional model after a colon; `lead` hands the feature back to the lead. Empty means every installed agent other than Claude, then `lead`.
config.retriesPerRung: How many times an agent may resubmit a feature after its checks fail before the feature moves to the next agent in the ladder.
config.agentConcurrency: The most features one agent works on at the same time, by agent id: for example `{ "codex": 3 }`. Useful when one subscription limits parallel sessions.
config.hotspots: Files that several features would all want to change, such as lock files. A plan may only change them in its scaffold. Globs are relative to the repository root.
config.stallMinutes: Tells the lead when a worker has not called any Facade tool for this many minutes.
config.closeVerifiedWorkers: Closes a worker's terminal once its feature passes its checks.
config.workerMode.interactive: Each worker is its agent's own interactive terminal UI: you can watch it, answer its prompts and take over.
config.workerMode.headless: Each worker runs in its agent's non-interactive mode where the agent has one, in a terminal that shows its progress. Facade records the tokens and cost it reports. Prompts the agent would ask are refused, so allow what the agent needs in its own settings first.
